rule: An Execution API FastAPI route's declared `status_code` must match every HTTP status code the handler actually returns; all non-default success codes must appear in the `responses` dict
trigger: FastAPI route decorator has `status_code=HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT` (or similar) but the handler also returns a different 2xx status, or a new status code is added to `responses` without updating the route's default `status_code`
rationale: Mismatched declared and actual status codes cause OpenAPI spec ambiguity and break clients that rely on the generated schema to understand what responses to expect

evidence.excerpt: route declares 204 No Content but handler also returns 200 OK for idempotent requests

rule: OpenTelemetry span names in the task execution path must embed the executing component (worker or triggerer) as a segment, e.g. `task_run.worker.{task_id}` or `worker.{task_id}`
trigger: New `tracer.start_span(name=...)` call in task execution routes uses a flat name like `task_run.{task_id}` without a component segment
rationale: Component-qualified span names allow workers and triggerers to be distinguished in traces; a flat `task_run.{task_id}` loses that context

rule: `VersionChange` subclass names must describe the schema migration performed (what field or model changes), not the behaviour of the old code being replaced
trigger: A class that subclasses `VersionChange` is named after what the previous code did (e.g. `ValidateSomething`) rather than after the data-model delta (e.g. `ChangeFooToBar`)
rationale: VersionChange subclasses exist solely to record upgrade/downgrade steps; naming them after old business logic misleads readers about the class's purpose

evidence.excerpt: name should describe upgrade/downgrade behavior, not token validation

rule: Do not add application-level mutex lock tables to guard writes that SQLite already serialises; skip the lock for SQLite backends
trigger: A new ORM model used as a mutex lock (e.g. `MutexLock`, `LockTable`) is added and `session.add`/`session.delete` are used around a critical section without a SQLite exemption
rationale: SQLite in WAL mode only allows one writer at a time, so a second application-level lock is redundant and adds unnecessary table overhead

evidence.excerpt: SQLite WAL mode only allows one writer; simply skip the lock table

rule: Use `if TYPE_CHECKING: assert x is not None` to narrow a variable's type within a branch rather than widening a downstream function's signature to accept `None`
trigger: A function's parameter type is widened to `T | None` solely because a caller cannot statically prove the value is non-None at the call site, and the value is known to be non-None at runtime
rationale: Adding `None` to a signature propagates the nullable type through callers and complicates the API; a `TYPE_CHECKING` assert narrows the type at the call site without runtime overhead

evidence.excerpt: `if TYPE_CHECKING: assert dialect_name is not None` avoids adding None to signature

rule: Prefer `session.scalar()` or `session.scalars().one()` over `session.get()` with a composite primary-key dict when querying ORM models
trigger: `session.get(ModelClass, {"key1": val1, "key2": val2})` is used to look up a model with a composite primary key
rationale: Composite-PK `session.get()` calls are fragile under schema changes; explicit `session.scalar(select(...).where(...))` makes the lookup columns visible and survives PK restructuring

evidence.excerpt: `session.get()` with composite PK is difficult to maintain if schema changes

rule: Setting `_AIRFLOW_PROCESS_CONTEXT` must be centralised in the `action_cli` decorator (when `check_db=True`), not scattered at individual CLI command call sites
trigger: A CLI command manually sets or reads `os.environ["_AIRFLOW_PROCESS_CONTEXT"]` inside the command body rather than relying on the `action_cli` decorator
rationale: Centralising context setup in the decorator ensures all `check_db=True` CLI commands get the correct server context; per-call-site fixes leave other commands vulnerable to the same missing-context bug

evidence.excerpt: setting context in `action_cli` decorator provides centralised solution matching PR description

rule: When adding a new keyword argument to a DB-command callable passed to `run_db_migrate_command`, all concrete implementations of that callable (including `BaseDBManager.upgradedb` and `FABDBManager.upgradedb`) must accept the new kwarg
trigger: A new `kwarg` is forwarded to a `command(...)` call inside `run_db_migrate_command` but the corresponding `upgradedb` methods on `BaseDBManager` or `FABDBManager` are not updated to accept it
rationale: `run_db_migrate_command` is shared by `fab-db migrate` and `db-manager migrate`; missing kwargs on any implementation cause a `TypeError` at runtime

evidence.excerpt: `fab-db migrate` and `db-manager migrate` will crash with unexpected keyword argument

rule: CLI date arguments that document a `yyyy-mm-dd` format must strictly validate that format and reject ISO-8601 datetime strings (e.g. timestamps with a `T` component)
trigger: A CLI argument parsed with `parsedate` or similar permissive parser is documented as accepting only `yyyy-mm-dd` but is not validated to reject datetime strings with time components
rationale: `parsedate` accepts timestamps like `2026-01-02T01:00:00`, silently bypassing date-only validation and producing unexpected range semantics

evidence.excerpt: `parsedate` could bypass validation with `2026-01-02T01:00:00` as input

rule: Only lazy-import a module inside a function body to break an import cycle; stdlib modules (`importlib`, `logging`) must always be imported at module top level
trigger: `import importlib`, `import logging`, or other stdlib modules appear inside a function body rather than at the top of the file
rationale: Per Airflow's AGENTS.md, lazy imports are reserved for breaking import cycles (e.g. `from airflow.providers_manager import ProvidersManager`); stdlib lazy imports are unnecessary overhead

evidence.excerpt: AGENTS.md says stdlib imports don't need to be lazy; only airflow import cycles do

rule: Bundle names persisted in `DagBundleModel` rows and emitted in REST API responses must be finalised before the first release that ships them; renaming afterwards requires a DB migration
trigger: A new auto-generated bundle name string (e.g. via an f-string concatenating package names) is introduced in bundle-discovery code that writes to `DagBundleModel`
rationale: Bundle names are stored in the database and returned by the REST API; any post-release rename requires a schema migration and breaks existing API consumers

evidence.excerpt: persisted in DagBundleModel rows and REST API responses; renaming requires a migration

rule: Columns added to SQLAlchemy `load_only()` clauses must be actually accessed by the downstream code that consumes the query result
trigger: A column is added to a `load_only(...)` call in a query-builder function but no code path that calls that function reads the newly added column attribute
rationale: Unnecessary columns in `load_only()` widen the SELECT unnecessarily, adding I/O and memory overhead with no benefit

evidence.excerpt: downstream references to the statement don't access `run_after` at all

rule: Use structlog keyword-argument style for all log calls; do not use `%s` positional format strings as log message arguments
trigger: A `log.info(...)`, `log.warning(...)`, or similar structlog call passes positional `%s` format arguments instead of keyword arguments for metadata fields
rationale: Airflow uses structlog throughout; `%s` format strings bypass structlog's structured key-value output and make log events harder to query and filter

evidence.excerpt: We use structlog, so provide short message with additional metadata with kwargs

rule: Config entries in `config.yml` must document the meaning of all special sentinel values (e.g. `0` meaning "disabled" or "unlimited") in the `description` field
trigger: A new config key with a numeric `default` of `0` (or another sentinel) is added to `config.yml` without the `description` explaining what `0` means
rationale: Operators reading `config.yml` have no other source of truth for what a default of `0` means; omitting it forces them to read source code

evidence.excerpt: description doesn't mention that `0` disables the limit

rule: A config `description` in `config.yml` must not reference Airflow features or model fields that do not exist at HEAD in the same PR
trigger: A new config key's `description` mentions a field name or feature (e.g. `TaskInstanceDTO.language`) that is not present in the codebase in the same PR
rationale: Config docs shipped before the feature they describe mislead operators into configuring something that has no effect, and the mismatch is hard to trace months later

evidence.excerpt: description references `language` field on TaskInstanceDTO which doesn't exist at HEAD

rule: A new single-entry config section must not be created as a top-level section in `config.yml`; place the entry in the `core` section following the precedent of `xcom_backend` and similar singleton settings
trigger: A new top-level YAML section is added to `config.yml` containing only one config key, when no further keys are planned
rationale: Single-entry top-level sections fragment the config namespace; Airflow convention is to place singleton backend/behaviour config keys under `core` (e.g. `xcom_backend`)

evidence.excerpt: Should not open a section for a single entry; add to core like `xcom_backend`
